content.text: All six preferred elements appear satisfied. Verifying the successor-transfer cross-reference is intact (Section 24.1 permits merger/acquisition assignment without consent) — it is.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The licence package sits at our preferred position. §13.1 grants the subscription right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" (affiliates and contractors covered, with no written-notice condition needed). §13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, satisfying the perpetual and irrevocable elements. §13.3 limits revocation or suspension to a "material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure," meeting the subscription-termination element, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor; that cross-reference holds because §24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets. The defined "Affiliate" (§1.1) is control-based and adequate. The only friction is §14.2, which describes the Deliverable licence as "revocable, non-transferable" and conflicts with §§13.2–13.3; consistent with the playbook we address revocability of Deliverable/IP rights once under the IP rule rather than flagging the same commercial term twice here.
